newsitem.title: ITALY: Burundi says end to sanctions would help aid.
newsitem.headline: Burundi says end to sanctions would help aid.

text.p: Burundi's Prime Minister Pascal Firmin Ndimira called on Thursday for an end to regional sanctions against his country, saying that lifting them would help a multinational aid effort for eastern Zaire.

Ndimira told Reuters in an interview that Burundian Hutu refugees caught up in the crisis should be encouraged to return home "but it would be better for the success of this operation that the embargo should be lifted."

Burundi's Tutsi-dominated military regime came to power on July 25 in a coup that brought Pierre Buyoya to power. Regional states including Tanzania, Kenya and Zaire imposed economic and political sanctions on Burundi six days later.

An estimated 150,000 Burundians are believed to be in eastern Zaire among some one million refugees, the others from Rwanda, caught in the crossfire of fighting. A multinational force is being put together to mount a relief operation.

Ndimira, who is in Rome for a food summit, said the "best way to success (of the operation) should be to get in touch with the powers in the area so that every party involved can give his commitment to help and to facilitate the operation."

Asked whether he would appeal for sanctions to be lifted in a summit speech on Friday, Ndimira said he did not want to divulge details but added: "Let's say that you cannot speak about food security without reference to economic sanctions."
